scope: Independent read-only final accounting audit of six completed evaluation runs: three policies, six selected questions, two repeats. No provider calls, backend writes, source/dataset edits or rescoring.

verification_issues: Minor: 'Mixing the two would blur separate workflows' is the author's inference, but it is framed as a recommendation and is acceptable.

Minor: the draft says it didn't run the example because the offline container can't import Weave. No code-run result in the payload supports that reason. The example is honestly labeled unrun, so this doesn't change the verdict, but the reason could be dropped or softened.

Minor: the sources do not state explicitly that the + New signal button sits on the Signals tab, or that the presets appear in the drawer under Tags. The answer infers both. This is a reasonable inference and does not need to be changed.
The answer honestly says it could not confirm whether existing saved conversations are scored retroactively. This is relevant because the user's conversations are already saved.
Minor: 'The scoring itself can take up to 30 seconds' loosely paraphrases the 30-second retry window and timeout. It is not a strict statement of per-request behavior on multi-tenant cloud.
Minor: 'HTTPS is required' is stated flatly. The source says HTTPS is required unless the deployment permits insecure HTTP, which doesn't affect multi-tenant cloud.

off_second_repeat_inspection.finding: All three assertions passed, but the answer cites nonexistent S7 for an additional self-managed ingest-sampling caveat. Deterministic citation resolution fails it.
All three assertions passed, but the final answer cites nonexistent S4 and S5. Deterministic citation resolution fails it, repeating the first-trial pattern.

Three of six assertions passed. Missing weave.init setup is real. The frozen Evaluation-versus-EvaluationLogger assertion is overly restrictive, and asynchronous-scoring evidence does not establish exact client-delivery ordering. No scores were changed.

method: Independently recomputed token costs with Decimal from each raw provider usage bucket, including explicit cache lifetimes and saved dated prices. Compared per-call values, per-run totals, shared ledger and final comparison.

Matched every attempt, prediction, score and standalone turn receipt. Verified exact assertion IDs, scoring arithmetic, source/config/prompt hashes, documentation page hashes, evaluation ancestry and unique provider IDs.

Rebuilt paired outcomes and case-group statistics from original score receipts without calling application aggregation helpers. Source bytes were checked against the original Git commit so subsequent documentation/UI work cannot relabel the measured implementation.
interpretation_limits: The six questions were selected for this capability pilot and are not an independent representative test sample. Thirty-six case-trials are eighteen repeated cells over six question groups, not thirty-six independent questions.

Reported standard errors describe variation across six question-level means (or six paired question-level differences). They are descriptive only, not calibrated population confidence intervals, significance tests or evidence of general reliability.

Off/support/coverage share the planner but differ in deterministic citation release checks, verifier calls and supplied evidence breadth. Off-versus-support cannot isolate an LLM-verifier effect, and support-versus-coverage is not a checklist-only intervention.
Model outputs are stochastic; arm order rotates between repeats, but cache state, provider load and same-family judge limitations remain potential confounders.
Frozen rubric remains unchanged despite known overly restrictive Evaluation-versus-EvaluationLogger wording and timing-order caveats. Raw verdicts are preserved; this audit does not regrade answers.

Agent latency sums all Agent.run turns in a case, excluding offline judging, corpus setup and harness overhead. Weave output.elapsed_seconds is final-turn-only; complete evaluation wall time is different.
Micro assertion fractions weight individual assertions. Weave scalar means weight each case fraction equally; they need not agree.

Costs cover returned agent and offline-judge usage once, at dated prices. They exclude Signals, tax, hosting, probes/calibration outside this pilot and any charges with unreturned usage; they are not an invoice.

Local accounting completion does not imply every public Weave summary has rendered. Recorded remote-sync exceptions and prior Compare N/A limitations are retained; this audit performs no backend repairs.
Case receipts contain evaluation/predict-and-score IDs and provider response IDs, but no direct judge Call ID.
